posts.title: Owning a Home is Not a Right
posts.description: What happens when a city changes the rules around rental deposits and criminal history? In this episode of Building a Better Dave , I share my perspective on Akron's recent housing measures, drawing on my own experience saving for an apartment and a home. Press play for a candid conversation about budgeting, housing access, and whether these new policies address the problems they're meant to solve. Why I Believe Financial Discipline Matters in Homeownership I look back on how my first wife and I saved for an apartment and, eventually, a house. By tracking what came in and what went out—and limiting some spending—we worked toward our goal. I also reflect on the disconnect I felt when a bank suggested we could afford a much more expensive home than I thought was realistic. Akron Rental Laws: Security Deposits and Application Fees I discuss Akron's changes allowing tenants to pay security deposits in installments over several months and banning rental application fees. posts.title: Stop Signs, Golf Clubs, and the KKK: Why We See What We're Looking For
posts.description: Stop Signs, Golf Clubs, and the KKK: Why We See What We're Looking For" If you see people as the enemy, you're going to find evidence of it everywhere, because that's exactly what you're looking for. That's the theme running through this episode, and I've got three ridiculous, infuriating examples to prove it. I open with a story from my restaurant days in my 20s, when I knew a guy so convinced everything was out to get him that I couldn't resist messing with him. I told him a stop sign is secretly Satanic: S-T-O-P, "Satan's the only power," and for about ten seconds, he actually bought it. It's a dumb bit, but it makes the point: when you're primed to see a threat, you'll see one, even in a stop sign. Then I get into the real outrage of the week. A golf club ad gets torched online because a husband tackles his wife to stop her from swinging a "possessed" driver, and somehow that becomes "promoting domestic abuse." posts.title: Quit Telling Me What To Think
posts.description: I expect the news to lean left or to lean right, and it drives me crazy. The one side calls the other side a bunch of names. We never really get the true story. It's all intended not to inform but more to entertain and to get a bunch of bullet points across. Now it's getting worse. When I was a little kid, I saw Gone with the Wind with my mother. It was her favorite movie because of Clark Gable, who was hot. I'm amazed she took me because the movie is almost four hours long, but I do remember there was an intermission because any males over 50 couldn't hold their pee that long, even in 1939. But now a fictional story has to have a disclaimer in the description or before you watch the movie on HBO. That's driving me crazy that people feel they have to inform me that slavery was bad. As bad as public school education is, we did get the point that slavery does not look like a lot of fun. I remember watching Roots and just being absolutely horrified.
